'''''Parapholis incurva''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] native to Europe, Asia and northern Africa, and widely [[introduced species|naturalised]] elsewhere. Common names include '''coast barbgrass''', '''curved sea hard grass''', '''curved hard-grass''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''sicklegrass''', '''curved sicklegrass''' and '''curved parapholis'''.

==Description==
It is a tufted annual [[bunchgrass]] up to 30 centimetres high, with green flowers.<ref name="FloraBase 516">{{FloraBase | name = ''Parapholis incurva'' (L.) C.E.Hubb. | id = 516}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
It was first published as ''Aegilops incurva'' by [[Carl Linnaeus]], and transferred into ''[[Parapholis]]'' by [[Charles Edward Hubbard]] in 1946.<ref name="APNI">{{APNI | name = ''Parapholis incurva'' (L.) C.E.Hubb. | id = 42464}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is widespread in the old world, occurring in northern Africa, Europe, and Asia. It has widely naturalised elsewhere.<ref name="GRIN 414951">{{GRIN | name = ''Parapholis incurva'' (L.) C.E.Hubb. | id = 414951}}</ref>
